get.description:
The Organization's own view of its spend limit: the ceiling, its own limit
beneath it, and what it has spent.

put.description: Set or clear the Organization's own spend limit, at or below its ceiling.

Set an Organization's LLM spend ceiling.

Platform-administered: an Organization cannot raise its own cap, which is the
whole point of it as a cost control. It can only set a lower limit of its own.

get.description:
Which of the Organization's Agents a spend limit would actually bind.

Agents created before the Organization had a LiteLLM team carry no team on their
key, so a limit does not apply to them until they are enrolled.

post.description:
Attach the Organization's existing Agent keys to its team.

Returns the resulting coverage rather than a success flag: partial enrollment is
an ordinary outcome and the administrator needs to see what is still uncovered.

get.description:
Return the Google OAuth authorize URL for the popup to navigate to.

``google_workspace`` is the only supported provider; its scopes are derived per
request from ``services`` (comma-separated) and ``read_only`` rather than being fixed
per provider. The retired per-service Google providers are rejected here rather than
silently served, so a stale caller fails loudly instead of consenting to scopes no
integration can use.

``client_id`` (optional) selects a user-supplied Google client; when omitted the
app-owned client from config is used. Only the client id is needed here — it is
public and travels in the authorize URL — while the matching secret is supplied
later, to ``/token``.

Validate the signed state and hand the raw authorization code to the opener.

The code→token exchange happens in ``/token`` (authenticated), so the client secret
never has to transit this unauthenticated redirect.

post.description:
Exchange the authorization code for a refresh token.

Uses the caller-supplied client id/secret when present (a user's own Google client),
otherwise the app-owned client from config. The secret is read from the request body
— it never appears in a URL, the authorize request, or our logs.

Also returns the scopes Google actually granted and, when an ``openid`` scope was
requested, the account's email address. Both are additive: callers predating them
(gmail, google_sheets) still read ``refresh_token`` and get ``email: null``.

ActivityTrigger.title: ActivityTrigger
ActivityTrigger.description:
What set a piece of work going.

Inferred from timing, not reported by the runtime: a wake with an inbound
message just before it is the Agent answering someone. Everything else ran
without a person — a cron, a heartbeat, or the Agent's own follow-up.

Every field is derived from the stored category or rebuilt from validated
fragments; no cluster text reaches this DTO. See `provisioning_errors.py`.

AgentRestorePointList.title: AgentRestorePointList
AgentRestorePointList.description:
The page, plus what the caller needs to decide whether capture is offered.

``total`` counts every row an Agent has, including PRE_RESTORE backups and
failed captures. The cap counts neither, so a client cannot derive its
remaining headroom from the page alone.

AgentSpendRead.title: AgentSpendRead
AgentSpendRead.description:
One Agent's slice of organization spend, for the ranked table.

`agent_id` is None for the unattributed bucket, kept in the ranking rather than
filtered out: hiding it would let the organization total silently exceed the sum
of the rows shown beneath it.

AgentTemplateSelection.title: AgentTemplateSelection
AgentTemplateSelection.description:
A configuration selection: the template pin, and optionally the skill pins
and runtime settings that must hold with it.

Required skill pins are validated against the assignments the Agent *will* have,
so a template and its own skills have to arrive in one request.

CommunicationPolicyDisposition.title: CommunicationPolicyDisposition
CommunicationPolicyDisposition.description:
The explicit result of provider payload admission.

A provider event can be observed without becoming a durable Communication
Delivery. Keeping that decision typed lets diagnostics explain why an event
stopped at the policy boundary instead of treating every empty envelope as
an indistinguishable success.

CostHistogramBucket.description:
One bar of the cost-per-call distribution.

`upper` is None for the final open-ended bucket — a handful of very expensive

MemberInviteResult.title: MemberInviteResult
MemberInviteResult.description:
Result of adding/resending an invite. ``invite_link`` is present only when a link
was actually issued — on an add that means a brand-new user, since anyone who already
exists keeps the one link their account already has.

MonthlyCostRead.title: MonthlyCostRead
MonthlyCostRead.description:
One calendar month of spend.

Months with no calls are returned as zero rather than omitted, so a quiet month
reads as a quiet month instead of silently closing the gap between its
neighbours. `month` is the first instant of the month in UTC.

OrganizationLlmBudgetRead.title: OrganizationLlmBudgetRead
OrganizationLlmBudgetRead.description:
What an Organization is allowed to know about its own spend limit.

Requires `cost.read`, so Owners and Admins only — the same audience as the rest
of the Organization's spend figures.

OrganizationLlmBudgetUpdate.title: OrganizationLlmBudgetUpdate
OrganizationLlmBudgetUpdate.description:
Platform-administered spend ceiling. Always an amount: an Organization can no
longer be uncapped, and an administrator who means "unlimited" sets a large one.

OrganizationLlmCoverageRead.title: OrganizationLlmCoverageRead
OrganizationLlmCoverageRead.description:
Whether this Organization's Agents are actually subject to its team budget.

Read live from the proxy rather than cached: a key detached by hand would make a
stored answer claim coverage the Organization does not have.

OrganizationMemberRead.title: OrganizationMemberRead
OrganizationMemberRead.description: A user's membership within one organization, for member-management UIs.

OrganizationOwnLlmBudgetUpdate.title: OrganizationOwnLlmBudgetUpdate
OrganizationOwnLlmBudgetUpdate.description: An Organization's own limit. Null follows the platform ceiling.

OrganizationSpendRead.title: OrganizationSpendRead
OrganizationSpendRead.description:
One organization's slice of platform spend.

`organization_id` is None for the unattributed bucket, which is kept in the
ranking rather than filtered out: hiding it would let the platform total silently
exceed the sum of the rows shown beneath it.

PlatformAgentDetailsRead.title: PlatformAgentDetailsRead
PlatformAgentDetailsRead.description:
What the Platform page shows when a Heaviest agents row is opened.

An explicit allowlist, per the Platform oversight ADR: identity and lifecycle, whether
the Agent is working, restarts and why the last one ended, and its usage. It carries no
log text, no free-text health reason and no failure detail; the failure summary is fixed
product copy chosen by category.

PlatformAgentResourceUsageRead.title: PlatformAgentResourceUsageRead
PlatformAgentResourceUsageRead.description:
One Agent's usage over the last day, as the Platform page shows it.

Mirrors the figures the Organization overview's panel shows, field for field, without
reusing its DTO. `availability` is about the source, `state` about the Agent.

PlatformAgentSeriesPoint.title: PlatformAgentSeriesPoint
PlatformAgentSeriesPoint.description:
One UTC day bucket of Agent inventory and activity.

`existing` is how many Agents were live at the end of that day and `created`
is how many were added during it — both reconstructed exactly from
created_at/deleted_at.

`active` is how many did observable work that day: sent or received a
message, or ran a tool. It is measured from telemetry rather than from
lifecycle events, so it answers "did this Agent do anything" rather than
"was its deployment meant to be up". Activity is always a lower bound on
running — an idle Agent that is up all day is active on none of them.

PlatformAgentStatsRead.title: PlatformAgentStatsRead
PlatformAgentStatsRead.description:
Agent inventory and activity.

Three deliberately separate numbers rather than one ambiguous "active":

- `total` — every Agent not soft-deleted, right now.
- `running` / `stopped` / `errored` — the current status split, right now.
  Read from the Agent row, so they reflect the last recorded state rather
  than liveness: an Agent whose pod died without anyone stopping it still
  counts as running. The three partition `total`.
- `active` — Agents with observable telemetry anywhere in the period. This is
  the honest activity measure, and the one the series tracks.

PlatformAgentUsagePoint.title: PlatformAgentUsagePoint
PlatformAgentUsagePoint.description: One Agent at one step. A missing reading is null, so a gap shows as a gap.

PlatformCapacityRead.title: PlatformCapacityRead
PlatformCapacityRead.description:
The namespace's ceilings and what is committed against them.

The ceilings are entered by a Platform Administrator, because the quota itself cannot
be read; the committed figures come from kube-state-metrics. They are always for the
whole namespace, whatever Organization the page is narrowed to. A quota caps limits and
requests alike, and a new pod is refused when any of the four would go over, so all four
are here, named as the quota names them.

PlatformCostRecordRead.title: PlatformCostRecordRead
PlatformCostRecordRead.description:
The platform admin's view of a call.

A separate type rather than an optional field on the org one, per the oversight
ADR's dedicated-read-model rule: the org surface must not be able to return an
organization name by accident.

PlatformCostSummaryRead.title: PlatformCostSummaryRead
PlatformCostSummaryRead.description: The org summary plus the figures only a platform admin sees.

PlatformMessageSeriesPoint.title: PlatformMessageSeriesPoint
PlatformMessageSeriesPoint.description: One bucket of chat volume, keyed by its UTC start instant.

PlatformOrganizationMemberRead.title: PlatformOrganizationMemberRead
PlatformOrganizationMemberRead.description:
Dedicated read model for Platform View oversight of an Organization's members,
kept separate from OrganizationMemberRead per the Platform Oversight ADR (no reuse
of Organization-scoped DTOs).

PlatformOrganizationRead.title: PlatformOrganizationRead
PlatformOrganizationRead.description:
Dedicated read model for Platform View: adds immutable Creator identity on top
of what OrganizationRead exposes to Organization members, per the Platform
Oversight ADR (no reuse of Organization-scoped DTOs).

PlatformOrganizationUserRead.title: PlatformOrganizationUserRead
PlatformOrganizationUserRead.description: Platform View membership read model with an allowlisted organization shape.

PlatformTemplateAdminSummary.title: PlatformTemplateAdminSummary
PlatformTemplateAdminSummary.description: One row of the Platform Admin authoring catalogue: a lineage plus its draft status.

PlatformTemplateDraftCreate.title: PlatformTemplateDraftCreate
PlatformTemplateDraftCreate.description: Starts a Draft Template Version for a brand-new lineage (no published version yet).

PlatformUsagePoint.title: PlatformUsagePoint
PlatformUsagePoint.description: All the selected Agents together at one step. A missing reading is null.

PlatformUserRead.title: PlatformUserRead
PlatformUserRead.description: Platform View user read model with allowlisted membership organizations.

PromptTokenDistribution.title: PromptTokenDistribution
PromptTokenDistribution.description:
How big the prompts were, across the window.

A high floor with a narrow spread is the fingerprint of a large static
context resent on every call, which is a different problem from a few long
conversations — and the averages alone cannot tell them apart.

ResourceUsageAvailability.title: ResourceUsageAvailability
ResourceUsageAvailability.description: Whether the numbers could be fetched at all. About the source, not the Agent.

ResourceUsageRange.title: ResourceUsageRange
ResourceUsageRange.description: How far back a chart looks. Capped at 14 days: Prometheus keeps 15.

ResourceUsageState.title: ResourceUsageState
ResourceUsageState.description: What the source knows about one Agent.

SharePointSignInRead.title: SharePointSignInRead
SharePointSignInRead.description: Who signed in and what the agent reaches. Also the agent's current SharePoint access.

SkillDraftUpdate.title: SkillDraftUpdate
SkillDraftUpdate.description:
Replace draft files and optionally stage metadata.

An omitted metadata field remains unchanged; an explicit ``null`` clears it.

SkillSummaryRead.title: SkillSummaryRead
SkillSummaryRead.description: A skill as the Skills UI sees it: lineage plus its latest published version.

SkillUpdate.title: SkillUpdate
SkillUpdate.description: Name-only edit. Content metadata changes go through draft/publish.

SkillVersionPin.title: SkillVersionPin
SkillVersionPin.description: An explicit skill version pin for an agent assignment.

SkillVersionRead.title: SkillVersionRead
SkillVersionRead.description: One immutable entry in a Skill lineage's version history.

StatsGranularity.title: StatsGranularity
StatsGranularity.description:
Bucket size for the series.

The value doubles as the postgres `date_trunc` unit and the
`generate_series` step, so it must stay lowercase and valid for both.

StatsPeriod.title: StatsPeriod
StatsPeriod.description: Reporting windows fixed by the AF-235 backlog: 7, 30, and 90 days.

TemplateSkillGroup.title: TemplateSkillGroup
TemplateSkillGroup.description:
An "at least one of" requirement group: the agent must be assigned at
least one skill from `skill_ids` at creation, and cannot drop below one
thereafter.

OAuth2PasswordBearer.description: Session access JWT or user-owned Personal API Key (abk_...), sent as a Bearer credential.
